subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

steps.tx: **Rotterdam criteria** establish the international diagnostic framework for polycystic ovary syndrome, requiring the presence of at least two of three cardinal features: oligo- or anovulation; clinical and/or biochemical signs of hyperandrogenism; and polycystic ovarian morphology on pelvic ultrasonography. Application of the criteria requires the strict exclusion of specific secondary mimicking etiologies including non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hyperprolactinaemia, thyroid dysfunction, and androgen-secreting ovarian or adrenal neoplasms.
steps.say: The Rotterdam criteria require at least two of three features: ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound. Secondary mimics like thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia, and adrenal hyperplasia must be formally excluded.

vis.caption: Rotterdam diagnostic criteria, ovarian follicular dynamics, and metabolic intervention targets. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Polycystic ovarian morphology** has been updated in international evidence-based guidelines using modern high-frequency transvaginal ultrasound transducers. The diagnostic threshold requires twenty or more follicles per ovary, measuring between two and nine millimetres in diameter, and/or an increased ovarian volume of ten millilitres or greater, in the absence of a dominant follicle or corpus luteum. Follicles characteristically arrange in a peripheral radial pattern around an expanded, hyperechoic central stroma.
steps.say: Modern ultrasound criteria define polycystic ovaries as twenty or more follicles measuring two to nine millimetres, or an ovarian volume of ten millilitres or more. They form a characteristic string-of-pearls around dense central stroma.

vis.title: International Consensus Ultrasound Criteria for PCO Morphology
rows: 10 mL or greater in either ovary
Examine when no cyst >10 mm present
Repeat scan if active corpus luteum seen

steps.tx: **Modified Ferriman-Gallwey score** provides the standardized clinical metric for quantifying the degree and distribution of hirsutism. The scoring system evaluates terminal, coarse, pigmented hair growth across nine androgen-sensitive body areas: upper lip, chin, chest, upper back, lower back, upper abdomen, lower abdomen, upper arms, and thighs. Each anatomical site is graded from 0 (absence of terminal hair) to 4 (extensive confluent growth). A total composite score of four to eight defines clinical hirsutism depending on racial ethnicity.
steps.say: The modified Ferriman-Gallwey score grades coarse terminal hair across nine androgen-dependent areas from zero to four. A score of four to eight, depending on ethnicity, confirms clinical hirsutism.

right.title: Terminal Hair (Hirsutism)
points: Driven by 5-alpha reductase conversion to DHT

steps.tx: **Insulin resistance** is present in up to seventy-five percent of women with polycystic ovary syndrome, independent of body mass index, driven by post-receptor defects in insulin signaling. Compensatory hyperinsulinaemia acts directly on the liver to suppress sex hormone-binding globulin, elevating free circulating testosterone. Furthermore, insulin acts through its own receptor and homologous IGF-1 receptors on ovarian theca cells to augment steroidogenesis. Up to ten percent of affected women develop type 2 diabetes by age forty.
steps.say: Insulin resistance affects most women with PCOS regardless of weight. The resulting hyperinsulinaemia suppresses liver SHBG, releasing free active testosterone, while directly stimulating ovarian theca cells to overproduce androgens.

nodes.label: Dual Target Action
nodes.sub: Suppresses hepatic SHBG and stimulates theca cells

nodes.label: Androgen Toxicity
nodes.sub: Hirsutism, ovulatory arrest, and metabolic syndrome

steps.tx: **Acanthosis nigricans** serves as a dependable cutaneous physical marker of profound, severe insulin resistance in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome. It presents as symmetrical, velvety, hyperpigmented, papillomatous plaques prominently distributed along the posterior neck, axillae, groin creases, and inframammary folds. High circulating concentrations of insulin cross-react with and activate insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) receptors on dermal fibroblasts and epidermal keratinocytes, stimulating localized epithelial hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis.
steps.say: Acanthosis nigricans is a telltale skin sign of severe insulin resistance. High circulating insulin stimulates keratinocyte IGF-1 receptors, causing velvety hyperpigmented plaques across the neck and axillae.

left.title: Acanthosis in PCOS
points: Velvety flexural plaques on neck and axillae
Improves with weight loss and metformin

right.title: Malignant Acanthosis
points: Rapid, explosive mucosal and palm involvement

steps.tx: **Endometrial cancer** risk is elevated three- to four-fold in women with chronic anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome. In the continuous absence of ovulation, the endometrium is deprived of cyclical progesterone-mediated differentiation and secretory shedding. Sustained, unopposed circulating estrogen stimulates constant, unmitigated endometrial glandular proliferation. This unremitting mitogenic stimulus leads sequentially from hyperplasia without atypia to atypical hyperplasia and well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma, mandating periodic withdrawal bleeding every three months.
steps.say: PCOS carries a four-fold increased risk of endometrial cancer. Without ovulation, there is no progesterone to oppose estrogen, causing relentless glandular growth. Induce a withdrawal bleed at least every three months to shed the lining.

nodes.label: Chronic Anovulation
nodes.sub: Absent corpus luteum and zero progesterone

steps.tx: **Lifestyle intervention** incorporating structured caloric restriction and regular aerobic exercise constitutes the mandatory first-line therapy for all overweight and obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome. A weight loss of just five to ten percent of total baseline body weight significantly reduces visceral adipose tissue, improves peripheral insulin sensitivity, lowers circulating bioavailable testosterone, and spontaneously restores regular ovulatory menstrual cycles and spontaneous fertility in over fifty percent of patients.
steps.say: Lifestyle modification is the foundation of management. A weight loss of just five to ten percent restores insulin sensitivity, drops free androgens, and restarts spontaneous ovulation in over half of overweight women.

vis.title: Therapeutic Hierarchy in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
rows: 5% to 10% weight loss via diet and exercise
Letrozole 2.5 to 5 mg daily on cycle days 3 to 7

steps.tx: **Spironolactone** at doses of fifty to two hundred milligrams daily serves as a potent anti-androgenic medication for persistent hirsutism failing six months of oral contraceptive therapy. It competitively blocks androgen receptors in target tissues and inhibits 5-alpha reductase, preventing conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone within pilosebaceous units. Because spironolactone causes feminization of a male fetus, it must always be co-prescribed with effective contraception, alongside monitoring of serum potassium for potential hyperkalaemia.
steps.say: Spironolactone blocks androgen receptors and 5-alpha reductase, clearing stubborn facial hair. Because it can feminize a male fetus, reliable contraception is mandatory, and serum potassium should be monitored periodically.

right.title: Safety and Precautions
points: Risk of male fetal genital feminization
Menstrual spotting if used without oral pill
